candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential; validate unexpected diagnostic/monitoring results and reduce risk from acting on inaccurate data
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — verifying an unexpected home blood glucose meter result
candidate.educational_objective: When a home glucose-meter result is unexpected or clinically discordant, verify testing technique by washing and drying the hands and repeating the measurement before acting on a potentially erroneous value.

options.A: Wash and dry the hands thoroughly, repeat the test using the meter and test-strip instructions, and seek further evaluation if the repeat result remains discordant with the clinical picture.
options.B: Immediately increase the insulin dose based on the single unexpected reading without repeating the test.
options.C: Ignore all unusually high meter readings when the client has no symptoms because asymptomatic results are unreliable.
options.D: Rinse the fingers with water but leave them wet before retesting because moisture improves capillary blood sampling.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. FDA guidance states that blood glucose meter accuracy depends partly on how the test is performed and specifically instructs users to wash and dry their hands and closely follow the meter instructions. ADA 2026 further states that a meter result that is discordant with the clinical picture should be retested and, if concern persists, confirmed by laboratory testing as appropriate. Residue on the fingers can contaminate a capillary sample, so repeating the test after proper hand preparation is safer than changing therapy from one unexpected value. B risks a medication error. C dismisses potentially important hyperglycemia. D is incorrect because hands should be dried before testing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Correct capillary glucose testing requires clean, dry hands and adherence to device instructions; an unexpected result should be repeated before treatment decisions are made, with further confirmation if discordance persists.
candidate.source_document_title: Blood Glucose Monitoring Devices; Diabetes Technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026

candidate.stem: A client using a home blood glucose meter obtains a reading that is much higher than expected shortly after handling fruit. The client has no symptoms of hyperglycemia. Which action should the nurse recommend first?
